GRADE 4 MATHEMATICS — TERM 1 EXAM

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Time: 64 minutes

INSTRUCTIONS
1. Answer all questions.
2. Use neat handwriting.
2. For multiple choice, write the correct letter only.
3. For short answers, write clearly in the spaces provided.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A: Multiple Choice

1. About Whole Numbers (10 at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. use place value and total value of digits up to tens of thousands in daily life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers (10 completely.
   C. Whole Numbers (10 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers (10.

2. About Whole Numbers (10 using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. read and write numbers up to 10,000 in symbols in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers (10 completely.
   C. Whole Numbers (10 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers (10.

3. About Whole Numbers (10 when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. read and write numbers up to 1,000 in words in day-to-day activities,
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers (10 completely.
   C. Whole Numbers (10 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers (10.

5. About Addition (8 at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. add up to two 4-digit numbers with single regrouping up to a sum of 10,000 in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Addition (8 completely.
   C. Addition (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Addition (8.

6. About Addition (8 using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. add up to two 4-digit numbers with double regrouping up to a sum of 10,000 in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Addition (8 completely.
   C. Addition (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Addition (8.

7. About Addition (8 when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. estimate sum by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Addition (8 completely.
   C. Addition (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Addition (8.

9. About Subtraction (8 at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. subtract up to 4-digit numbers without regrouping in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Subtraction (8 completely.
   C. Subtraction (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Subtraction (8.

10. About Subtraction (8 using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. subtract up to 4-digit numbers with regrouping in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Subtraction (8 completely.
   C. Subtraction (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Subtraction (8.

11. About Subtraction (8 when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. estimate difference by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different contexts,
   B. Learners should ignore Subtraction (8 completely.
   C. Subtraction (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Subtraction (8.

13. About Multiplication (8 at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. multiply up to a two-digit number by multiples of 10 in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication (8 completely.
   C. Multiplication (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication (8.

14. About Multiplication (8 using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. multiply up to a two-digit number by two-digit number with and without regrouping,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication (8 completely.
   C. Multiplication (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication (8.

15. About Multiplication (8 when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. multiply up to a two digit number by 100 in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Multiplication (8 completely.
   C. Multiplication (8 is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Multiplication (8.

17. About Division at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. divide up to a two-digit number by a one-digit number with and without remainder,
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

18. About Division using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. divide up to a three-digit number by 100
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

19. About Division when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. relate multiplication of numbers to division of same numbers in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Division completely.
   C. Division is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Division.

21. About Fractions at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. identify the numerator and denominator in a fraction in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

22. About Fractions using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. represent a fraction with denominators not exceeding 12 as part of a whole and as part of a group,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

23. About Fractions when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. identify different types of fractions in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

25. About Decimals at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. identify a tenth and a hundredth inreal-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

26. About Decimals using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. represent decimals using decimalnotation in given situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

27. About Decimals when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. identify place value of decimals upto hundredths in real life,
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

29. About Use of letters at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. represent information using letters in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Use of letters completely.
   C. Use of letters is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Use of letters.

30. About Use of letters using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. form simple expressions to represent real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Use of letters completely.
   C. Use of letters is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Use of letters.

31. About Use of letters when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. simplify expressions with up to two unknowns representing real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Use of letters completely.
   C. Use of letters is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Use of letters.

SECTION B: Short Answers

4. Give two examples of how you can use Whole Numbers (10 at the market in your county.

8. Give two examples of how you can use Addition (8 at the market in your county.

12. Give two examples of how you can use Subtraction (8 at the market in your county.

16. Give two examples of how you can use Multiplication (8 at the market in your county.

20. Give two examples of how you can use Division at the market in your county.

24. Give two examples of how you can use Fractions at the market in your county.

28. Give two examples of how you can use Decimals at the market in your county.

32. Give two examples of how you can use Use of letters at the market in your county.
